elements.element: This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of New York.
elements.evidence: Section 28.1 expressly provides that the Agreement is governed exclusively by the laws of the State of New York.

elements.element: The state courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction.
elements.evidence: Section 28.2 grants exclusive jurisdiction to the state courts located in New York County, New York. The injunctive-relief provision is limited to “those courts,” so it does not create an outside-forum exception.

elements.element: The federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction.
elements.evidence: Section 28.2 grants exclusive jurisdiction to the federal courts located in New York County, New York. The injunctive-relief provision is limited to “those courts,” so it does not create an outside-forum exception.

elements.element: The governing law is the law of Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: Section 28.1 selects New York law, not any of the permitted fallback laws.

elements.element: The selected courts correspond to the fallback governing law: Delaware courts for Delaware law, California courts for California law, or the courts of London for the laws of England and Wales.
elements.evidence: Section 28.2 selects state and federal courts in New York County rather than Delaware courts, California courts, or the courts of London.

result.reason: The redline fully implements the preferred New York governing-law and exclusive-forum position. It removes the conflicting Singapore forum language and confines temporary injunctive relief to the designated New York courts, preserving genuine exclusivity. The changes are limited to those needed to reach the preferred position and introduce no operative contradiction.
